observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a used engine block with an attached manual/automatic transaxle (gearbox) and a separate differential/transfer-case style housing protruding at the bottom, consistent with a 4WD drivetrain layout.
A turbocharger-like component is visible at the top right of the engine in photo 0.
Surface oxidation/light rust and grime are visible on the block, bell housing, and exposed metal surfaces in both photos.
No engine code, part number, or Toyota branding is legibly visible on the block, gearbox casing, or any sticker in either photo.
A watermark 'ALEX AUTO ALEXANDER' and a 'POSTED ON JIJI' overlay appear across both images; these are seller-added text, not proof of the part's identity or condition.
No wiring harness, sensors, or intake manifold completeness can be fully verified; some hoses and connectors are dangling loose in photo 0.
No video, startup clip, or compression/leakdown test shown; engine state (running or not) cannot be assessed from stills.

identity.kind: used engine and gearbox assembly with transfer case/differential housing (claimed Toyota Highlander fitment)

Gearbox connector/pin count is not visible or countable in either photo.
Photo 1 shows a differential/transfer-case style housing with CV-joint ends at the bottom, which is plausible for 4WD, but no badge or part tag confirms the drivetrain spec.
No Toyota badge, VIN tag, or OEM part sticker is legible in either photo.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (compression, timing, bearings).
risks.proof: A start-up video with the engine idling, plus a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Gearbox may be damaged, seized, or not shifting correctly.
risks.proof: A video of gear engagement or a bench test clip with the gearbox turning through all gears.

risks.risk: Assembly may be incomplete (missing sensors, wiring harness ends, intake parts, turbo seals).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the wiring harness connectors, turbo mounting, and intake manifold from multiple angles.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete, deduct for missing ancillaries

risks.risk: Visible surface rust/oxidation could indicate prolonged outdoor storage or water exposure affecting internals.
risks.proof: Close-up of cylinder bores via spark plug hole or oil dipstick condition photo/video.
risks.if_unproven: priced as yard-stored, condition discount applied

risks.risk: Mismatched or incompatible gearbox/engine pairing for the claimed Highlander trim (engine code and transmission type must match exactly).
risks.proof: Legible photo of the engine code stamp and gearbox ID plate/tag.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified Toyota V6 assembly, not Highlander-specific

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine code stamp/casting mark on the block.
Clear close-up photo of the gearbox ID tag or sticker.
A start-up video with audio of the engine running.
Photos of the full wiring harness, sensors, and intake components from the front and sides.
A video of the gearbox being turned/shifted through gears on a bench.
response.reason: The listing shows a used Toyota-style V6 engine with attached transaxle and a transfer case/differential housing consistent with a 4WD setup, but no engine code, gearbox tag, or Toyota marking is legible in either photo, and there is no running or shifting proof, so all seller claims remain unverified; this is priced at worst case as an untested, unconfirmed-fitment used engine/gearbox assembly.
